_comment: Default runtime settings. Override by pointing BEP_CONFIG at your own JSON file, or by placing bep.config.json in the working directory; values are deep-merged over these.

ai.system_prompt: You are a senior BIM information manager drafting sections of a BIM Execution Plan under ISO 19650. You write in the plain, committing register of a contract document: specific, checkable statements with named responsibilities, dates and tolerances. Never write filler such as 'TBD', 'as required' or 'industry best practice'. Never invent a fact that contradicts the project context you are given; where a fact is genuinely unknown, write a concrete placeholder in angle brackets such as <confirm with the appointing party> so the author can see exactly what to fill in. Return only the requested content, with no preamble, no headings and no explanation of what you did.

modes.draft: Draft this field from scratch for the project described above.
modes.improve: Rewrite the author's current text so it is specific and auditable. Keep every fact they stated; add the commitments a reviewer would expect to see. Do not pad the word count.
modes.expand: Keep the author's current text and extend it with the detail it is missing. Return the complete field, not just the addition.
modes.critique: Do not rewrite. List, as short bullets, exactly what an ISO 19650 auditor would reject in the current text and what is missing.

lod._comment: Each level lists the IFC classes that may appear at that level of development, and how they are drawn. 'geometry': mesh renders the tessellated solid; bbox renders the element's bounding box, which is how a LOD 100/200 massing model is meant to read.

100.label: LOD 100 — Symbolic massing
100.note: Overall form, area, height and orientation only. Elements are shown as massing boxes.

200.label: LOD 200 — Generic systems
200.note: Generic elements with approximate size, shape, location and orientation.

300.label: LOD 300 — Specific assemblies
300.note: Specific elements accurate in size, shape, location and orientation. The normal coordination level.

350.label: LOD 350 — Interfaces and connections
350.note: Adds the parts needed for coordination with adjacent trades: supports, fittings, terminals.

400.label: LOD 400 — Fabrication and assembly
400.note: Detailed enough for fabrication and installation, including fixings and discrete components.

500.label: LOD 500 — Verified as-built
500.note: Field-verified representation. Everything present in the model is shown.

sections._comment: Which field in each framework drives the viewer's level of development. 'column' names the table column holding the LOD value; omit it for a plain field.

viewer._skip_comment: Classes never written into the viewer payload. Openings are voids, not objects: every viewer hides them.

ids._comment: Export of the plan's level-of-information-need table as a buildingSMART IDS 1.0 document, and the check of attached models against it. Every key can be overridden per run with bep --set ids.<key>=<value>; the common ones also have their own ids export / ids check option.
ids._ifc_version_comment: ifc_version is the target schema list for an export. When a model is checked and ifc_version_from_model is true, the model's own schema is the target instead. schema_aliases maps what a file header says onto the IDS schema name.
ids._milestone_comment: Empty exports every row of the table as one IDS. A value keeps only the rows whose milestone column (sources.<framework>.columns.stage) equals it, so a Stage 3 model is not checked against Stage 4 requirements.
ids._pset_comment: A property written as Pset_DoorCommon.FireRating in the table is required in that property set. One written without a set goes into default_pset.
ids._include_subtypes_comment: An IDS entity facet matches its class exactly. When true, a requirement on IfcWall also applies to its instantiable subtypes (IfcWallStandardCase), those defined in every target schema.
ids.description_format: Generated from the BIM Execution Plan ({framework}).

auth._comment: HTTP basic authentication. Off unless both user and password are set, here or via BEP_AUTH_USER / BEP_AUTH_PASSWORD. Needed for any deployment reachable from outside your own machine: the app has no other access control.

cli._comment: What bep config prints in its summary. Any dotted settings path may be listed.
